statement: A secret shown in dispute arguments is learned by every hosted Entity, as one shown by SecretRevealed is. The chain pays a payment clause when its secret is in the arguments of a dispute op before the clause's deadline (DeltaTransformer applyPayment, 294-299) and logs no SecretRevealed for it, so a hub that forwarded the lock would fail it back upstream while the payee was paid downstream. Two places carry such arguments. DisputeStarted logs the starter's two argument blobs (initial and counter) in its own data, so the watcher reads their secrets from the log. DisputeFinalized logs only finalizationEvidenceHash, a hash of the initial body hash, the final nonce, both sides, and the hashes of the starter's blob, the other side's blob and the signature; the blobs are in the input of the transaction. The Host fetches the input of each transaction that carried a start or a finalize of an Account a hosted Entity is a party to (a stranger's dispute is not read; eth_getTransactionByHash, once per transaction per poll), reads it with the ABI cursors as the contract reads it (processBatch, then the batch's finalize op; or a tower's watchtowerCounterDispute, whose params the contract finalizes with an empty signature, so its evidence hash is over one), and takes the secrets of the op whose evidence hash is the logged one, from both blobs: the evidence hash authenticates the op, so a secret is never taken from an op the log is not about. The Depository authorizes a batch by its Hanko, not by its sender (Depository.sol 340-348), so the call need not be the top of the transaction: a relay contract, a multicall or an `execute(target, data)` carries it in its own arguments. A transaction to the Depository is that one call: its input is read exactly by its ABI layout, from its first byte, and what follows the call's own components is ignored, so look-alike calls appended to it can never hide it and no scan is made. Only the input of a transaction to another contract is scanned: every place in it that begins with the processBatch or the tower's selector, at any offset, within a budget (an input of at most 1 MiB, at most 64 distinct ops; past it the scan is not made or read, loudly as unread), is read as a call, and what a call must prove is the same wherever it was found (the evidence hash, or for a start the body hash, the log names), so a call whose op has another hash is ignored. When no such call holds the op the Host asks the node for a call trace of the transaction (debug_traceTransaction with the callTracer, once per poll) and reads the input of each call whose target is the Depository, however deep. A node with no call trace says so with the method missing (JSON-RPC code -32601, or the texts of the clients that give no code: `Method not found`, geth's `the method debug_traceTransaction does not exist/is not available`, `Unsupported method`, `method not supported`) and that is an answer, not a fault; so is a trace that is not a tree of calls or is deeper than the EVM goes: no trace, so the finalize is told unread and the delivery goes on, because one counterparty transaction must not blind the watcher for good. Nothing else is taken for a missing method: an error that says only that something is not available, too big, a timeout, a missing trie node or unavailable historical state may clear, and is a fault of the node that the retry budget below bounds. A trace has no cap of a number chosen here: its limits are the EVM's, a transaction holds as many frames as its gas pays for and a call stack is at most 1024 deep, so it is walked a level at a time (never recursively) and every frame whose target is the Depository is read, a finalize as the last of 100000 frames or at depth 1024 included; only a tree deeper than the EVM goes is no trace; the manifest's Sepolia provider, ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com, answers -32601 to debug_traceTransaction and to trace_transaction (probed 10-02 on a real transaction), anvil answers both a callTracer trace (skeleton S10 reads the real finalize's). A node that may hold value (WatchConfig.value) is started only on a provider that answers debug_traceTransaction with the callTracer: the daemon asks once at boot with debug_traceTransaction and the callTracer on a real transaction of a recent block (the first transaction of the newest of the head's last 16 blocks that holds one: on a fork it is one mined after the fork point, since the fork's past is the upstream's to trace; when none holds one, debug_traceCall on a call of the Depository at the head, the same namespace and tracer) and refuses with no_call_trace when the method is missing (anvil answers, publicnode answers -32601, probed 10-02), so a provider that traces calls but not transactions does not pass; a relay that builds its call at run time leaves no selector to scan, so the notice alone does not save the amount a hub would lose, and a no-value run still starts. A transaction the node answers null for (it does not know it: a backend that has not indexed a young one, or a pruned node that will never give an old one, answer alike), or cannot give (its input, or its trace when the input held nothing), is a port fault that stalls the delivery at that block: the events before it are told, those from its block on wait and the read is tried again at the next poll, because a finalize's secrets must reach the Entity before the epoch advance it made and no event may be told out of its order. The wait is bounded: each transaction has a budget of 24 polls (MOST_TRIES), one counted against it only by a poll that reached its reads, so the head, the blocks and the logs were answered and the transaction's own read is the one that failed (a node that is down costs none); the Host carries the tries from one poll to the next and forgets a transaction it read or passed. The wait has an age bound as well, whichever comes first: a transaction the node still fails, after at least 3 failed polls (one failure of a node catching up is retried), more than `hold` blocks after its block became final (head - block - depth > hold) is told unread though it has tries left. `hold = hop - slack - lag - depth - 1` in J heights, with `hop = reserve + lag` the least a hub's inbound and onward deadlines differ by (paybook `hopOf`), `slack` the deployment's slack in heights (ceil of the time map's slackSeconds over its blockSeconds: the chain counts a payee's reveal until the onward deadline's second plus the slack, so it may reach the chain that many blocks after the deadline), `depth` the blocks the node waits before it reads a block and one more for the block that carries the reveal, and `lag` the blocks before the inbound deadline by which the hub's answer upstream must land. A reveal that reaches the chain last is then heard late by at most `hold` blocks and the hub can still claim upstream; a later event (a secret another payee shows) behind a stalled transaction is held no longer than it. A node whose configuration leaves `hold` below zero (slack above reserve - depth - 1) is refused at boot (`hold_below_zero`): no wait is safe. The slack is a node setting (WatchConfig.slack) until the deployment's time map is wired into the node's configuration. Until the bound passes a transaction a counterparty picked still holds every later event of every Account (owed: stall per Account, own PR). A poll in which every read fails (the head, the blocks, the logs) is a fault of the node, costs no tries, and stalls. A transaction that spent them is told unread, loudly (j_finalize_unread, or j_start_unread for a start), and the delivery goes on, so a pruned transaction is told unread once they are spent, and the node says so while it waits: a notice `watch_stalled` names the transaction and the provider's reason when a stall begins;  so a provider that fails one transaction for good (the same unknown error forever) cannot hold back every later block, a later SecretRevealed among them. A blob is `abi.encode(bytes[])`, one `abi.encode(Arguments{uint16[] fillRatios; bytes32[] secrets})` per clause of the proof body (DeltaTransformer decodeTransformerArgumentListStrict, Account.sol _decodeTransformerArgumentList; the skeleton's S10 asks the deployed DeltaTransformer to decode a blob and the node's decoder reads the same secret); a blob that is not that has no secrets (the contract reads it as empty). Each secret is told as `j_secret` to every hosted Entity, ahead of the event that follows it: a start's before its j_dispute, a finalize's before the epoch advance the finalize made (so before the holds that advance dissolves, R-HOLD-DISSOLVE; a finalize with no advance in the batch tells them before itself). The Entity's paybook turns a secret into a pass-up by its hash on any Account (R-DISPUTE-FREEZE), so a secret that opens no lock it forwarded changes nothing. Every read is bounded by what the contract accepts: one finalization and eight starts in a batch, 64 KiB of arguments, 128 tokens, 32 clauses, 128 allowances a clause (the contract takes at most as many allowances as deltas, and deltas as tokens: Account.sol 1206-1215), 176 KiB of clause bytes, 256 KiB of encoded batch or of tower call data (Depository.sol 354, 475); a batch, a blob or a list past them is one the Depository would revert, so it is not read (told as unread, or no body). A direct call has no cap on the input as a whole: bytes after the call's own components are no concern of the contract's, so a finalize padded with 1.3 MB of zeros is read like any other. A wrapper's input with more than 64 distinct ops (a flood of look-alike calls is not read, loudly, never half read), and offsets that alias one op many times cost one read. A finalize that neither the input, wherever a wrapper put the call, nor the call trace gives an op with the logged hash cannot be read: its parties are told `j_finalize_unread` naming the transaction (notice `finalize_unread` with the Account and the transaction, no fact changes) after `j_dispute_over`, so the owner knows a secret may have been shown unseen;  Unread is a notice and not a safe state: a hub that never learns the secret fails the lock back upstream while the payee was paid downstream, and the amount is lost; an operator whose provider has no call trace has no cover against a wrapper but the scan of the input. the watcher is not stopped for it, because a counterparty could wrap a finalize on purpose. A secret shown in the starter's counter blob is read though the chain uses that blob only if the counter is the one selected: reading more only hands a hub a real preimage. The start's transaction is read the same way for the body the start revealed (the contract has the starter reveal the exact signed body, `InitialDisputeProof.initialProofbody`): the Host takes the start op whose `proofbodyHash` is the logged one and keeps its body only if it hashes to that hash, so a body is never believed on the word of the bytes; the Entity keeps it on the dispute against it (`against.body`, re-checked against the logged hash) and a non-starter with nothing newer, or whose counter lapsed, finalizes the opening state with it when no state of its own has that body (R-DISPUTE-WATCH). A start of an Account a hosted Entity is a party to, whose input is unreadable (no op of the input, of a call in it or of the trace has the logged body hash), is told without a body and then as `j_start_unread` to the party that did not start it (notice `start_unread` with the Account and the transaction, no fact changes): without the body the Entity cannot answer the dispute by finalizing with it, and the owner is told so rather than left to wait; the starter's own start needs no body and no notice. The scan of an input compares a first byte at each offset and reads each input once per poll however many logs name its transaction (a 1 MiB input is scanned in tens of milliseconds, not seconds). Not here: the body of a counter's calldata (the finalized offdelta in the notices: owed), a relayed finalize on a real chain with a hostile payee (owed: S9, the dispute-clause step, needs a harness-built finalize), and secrets in a counter dispute (a counter proof carries no arguments).
source: Review A B4 on #162; coordinator audit of #162 (A: calldata PR); DeltaTransformer.sol 294-299; Depository.sol finalizationEvidenceHash (975-1006); builder 10-02; coordinator audit of #167 (B1 encoding, B2 bounds, B3 tower); coordinator relay-hole finding on #167
